sentences.en: TUTOR: Thanks for coming along, Nadia and Fergus. So this is a chance for you to give us some feedback about different aspects of your course. What would you like to begin with?
sentences.zh: TUTOR: 感谢你们的到来，纳迪亚和弗格斯。今天这次会议是你们就课程不同方面提供反馈的好机会。你们想先从哪方面开始？

sentences.en: NADIA: I've enjoyed the sessions on food safety. There was some information there that I found really surprising, although some was stuff I knew already, like the rise in rates of obesity.
sentences.zh: NADIA: 我很喜欢关于食品安全的课程。其中有些信息让我感到非常意外，不过也有一些内容是我原本就了解的，比如肥胖率上升的问题。

sentences.en: FERGUS: Yeah, that's been in the news a lot. But I hadn't realised that unsafe food causes more than 200 different diseases.
sentences.zh: FERGUS: 是啊，这在新闻中报道得很多。但我之前并不知道不安全食品会导致200多种不同的疾病。

sentences.en: NADIA: No. I'd no idea it was that many. And speaking of diseases, I knew resistance to antibiotics is on the increase, but I didn't know why...
sentences.zh: NADIA: 不知道。我完全没想到会有这么多。说到疾病，我知道抗生素耐药性正在加剧，但一直不清楚原因……

sentences.en: FERGUS: ... that it's partly because when animals are treated with antibiotics then consumed by humans. the antibiotics get into the food chain. I had no idea about that either.
sentences.zh: FERGUS: ……原因之一是动物在接受抗生素治疗后被人食用，抗生素便由此进入食物链。这一点我之前也完全不知道。

sentences.en: NADIA: Then the sessions provided a lot of information about plastic pollution from food packaging in the ocean, but I think that most of us were already aware of that.
sentences.zh: NADIA: 接着，课程还提供了大量关于食品包装塑料污染海洋的信息，但我觉得我们大多数人对此早已有所了解。

sentences.en: FERGUS: Yeah. But I thought we could have done more on how much food is thrown away unnecessarily through fear of it being out of date, that was only mentioned in passing.
sentences.zh: FERGUS: 是的。不过我认为，我们本可以更深入地探讨一下因担心食品过期而被不必要丢弃的现象——课程中仅一笔带过而已。

sentences.en: TUTOR: OK, I'll bear that in mind. What did you think about the sessions from visiting lecturers, Fergus?
sentences.zh: TUTOR: 好的，我会把这点记下来。弗格斯，你对客座讲师的授课内容有什么看法？

sentences.en: FERGUS: For me the most interesting one was about that project to prevent companies giving incorrect information to consumers about food.
sentences.zh: FERGUS: 对我而言，最有趣的一场讲座是关于一项旨在防止企业向消费者提供错误食品信息的项目。

sentences.en: TUTOR: Ah, food fraud, yes.
sentences.zh: TUTOR: 啊，就是食品欺诈问题，没错。

sentences.en: FERGUS: I thought it was really good to address a problem that's faced by so many different groups - people with special religious rules. as well as vegetarians and vegans.
sentences.zh: FERGUS: 我觉得能直面这样一个影响众多不同群体的问题，非常有意义——例如遵守特定宗教饮食规则的人群，以及素食者和纯素食者。

sentences.en: NADIA: And those with allergies.
sentences.zh: NADIA: 还有对某些食物过敏的人群。

sentences.en: FERGUS: Yeah. And another thing, we've had effective ways of analysing DNA for some time now and these can easily be applied to analysing food. But what the researchers succeeded in doing was to ensure that these tests were carried out at different stages in the food's journey from the producer to the consumer.
sentences.zh: FERGUS: 没错。另外，我们已拥有有效的DNA分析技术多年，这些技术很容易应用于食品分析。但研究人员成功之处在于，确保这些检测在食品从生产者到消费者整个流通过程的不同阶段均得以实施。

sentences.en: NADIA: So they knew that the food actually came from the place it was supposed to, and had the ingredients it was meant to.
sentences.zh: NADIA: 因此他们能够确认食品确实来自其标示的产地，并含有其所宣称的成分。

sentences.en: FERGUS: Exactly. So customers can be confident about what they buy.
sentences.zh: FERGUS: 没错。这样消费者就能对自己所购食品充满信心。

sentences.en: NADIA: And the researchers had a good system for publicising their findings too.
sentences.zh: NADIA: 而且研究人员还建立了一套良好的体系来公开发布他们的研究成果。

sentences.en: FERGUS: Well, I thought there were some problems with that, actually.
sentences.zh: FERGUS: 嗯，实际上我觉得这方面存在一些问题。

sentences.en: TUTOR: OK. And do you have any recommendations for new topics that we could include in the course?
sentences.zh: TUTOR: 好的。那么，你们有没有什么建议，比如课程中可新增哪些主题？

sentences.en: NADIA: Well, I'm interested in how crop yields can be increased without damaging the environment.
sentences.zh: NADIA: 我对如何在不破坏环境的前提下提高农作物产量很感兴趣。

sentences.en: FERGUS: But we've already done quite a bit on that - but not so much on the seafood industry. where stocks are in danger of being overexploited as a food source unless we can find ways of keeping stocks up.
sentences.zh: FERGUS: 但我们在这方面已经讲得相当多了——而对海产品产业的关注却相对不足。若不能找到方法维持鱼类资源，作为食物来源的海产储量正面临过度捕捞的危险。

sentences.en: NADIA: Yes. that'd be a good topic. And I'm interested in the idea of a personalised approach to diet, now we have the technology to analyse exactly what individuals need.
sentences.zh: NADIA: 是的，那会是个不错的主题。而且我现在对个性化饮食理念很感兴趣，因为我们现在已有技术可以精确分析每个人的具体需求。

sentences.en: FERGUS: That sounds more like a medical topic than food science.
sentences.zh: FERGUS: 这听起来更像是医学话题，而非食品科学。

sentences.en: NADIA: OK. What about sessions on the variety of food and eating habits around the world? That's very relevant nowadays.
sentences.zh: NADIA: 好吧，那关于全球各地食物种类与饮食习惯的专题讲座如何？这在当今非常相关。

sentences.en: FERGUS: Yes. I think the whole class would be interested in that.
sentences.zh: FERGUS: 是的，我觉得全班同学都会对此感兴趣。

sentences.en: NADIA: Then there's technological stuff. things like 3D printing of food and smart packaging.
sentences.zh: NADIA: 然后还有技术类内容，比如食物3D打印和智能包装。

sentences.en: FERGUS: Mmm - maybe too specialist.
sentences.zh: FERGUS: 嗯——可能过于专业了。

sentences.en: TUTOR: Now, I'm particularly interested in your project - the one where you developed a new food product. So talk me through the stages... first you had to decide on your initial aim.
sentences.zh: TUTOR: 现在，我对你们的项目特别感兴趣——就是你们开发了一款新型食品的那个项目。所以请向我介绍一下各阶段……首先，你们需要确定最初的目标。

sentences.en: FERGUS: We decided we wanted to create something people could eat on the go rather than in a restaurant.
sentences.zh: FERGUS: 我们决定要创造一种适合边走边吃的食物，而不是只能在餐厅里享用的食物。

sentences.en: NADIA: Yeah so we chose falafel, which was originally a Middle Eastern snack.
sentences.zh: NADIA: 对，所以我们选了鹰嘴豆饼（falafel），它原本是一种中东小吃。

sentences.en: FERGUS: 023/24 025/26 025/26 We made up our minds about that pretty quickly. I know some students found it a lot harder to choose, and wasted a lot of time.
sentences.zh: FERGUS: 023/24 025/26 025/26 我们很快便就此达成一致。我知道有些同学在选择时困难得多，还浪费了很多时间。

sentences.en: NADIA: Then we had to do the literature review. We hadn't done one of these before so. the handout with advice for the project was very useful here.
sentences.zh: NADIA: 接着我们要做文献综述。我们之前从未做过这类工作，因此项目指南中提供的建议在此处非常有用。

sentences.en: FERGUS: Yes. especially the advice on how to present the information. Then product development, actually deciding what we'd use to make the falafel, and for me the interesting thing about that was that we wanted it to be something a bit different from an ordinary falafel.
sentences.zh: FERGUS: 是的，尤其是关于如何呈现信息的建议。然后是产品开发阶段，即实际确定制作鹰嘴豆饼所用的原料；而对我来说，这一阶段有趣之处在于：我们希望成品与普通鹰嘴豆饼略有不同。

sentences.en: NADIA: We really made the right choice when we finally decided to use jackfruit, even though it wasn't something that either of us had ever tasted before.
sentences.zh: NADIA: 当我们最终决定采用菠萝蜜时，确实做出了正确的选择，尽管在此之前我们俩都从未尝过这种食材。

sentences.en: FERGUS: Yeah, like the name tells you, it's a fruit but actually it's really good in savoury dishes. The product production, working out how to make the falafel, was harder than I expected because I'd never made them before.
sentences.zh: FERGUS: 没错，正如其名所示，它是一种水果，但实际上非常适合用于咸味菜肴。产品制作阶段——即研究如何制作鹰嘴豆饼——比我预想的更难，因为我此前从未做过这种食物。

sentences.en: NADIA: It was mostly trial and error. We started off with the basic recipe and then experimented and when it went wrong...
sentences.zh: NADIA: 这基本上靠反复试验。我们先从基础食谱入手，再不断尝试；一旦失败……

sentences.en: FERGUS: ... which it did a lot of the time...
sentences.zh: FERGUS: ……而这种情况经常发生……

sentences.en: NADIA: ... we just moved on and kept adapting it and in the end it turned out fine and we had a lot of fun.
sentences.zh: NADIA: ……我们就直接继续推进，不断调整改良，最终结果还不错，而且整个过程也充满乐趣。

sentences.en: FERGUS: We did!
sentences.zh: FERGUS: 确实如此！

sentences.en: TUTOR: Thank you. Well, your project was a very good....
sentences.zh: TUTOR: 谢谢。嗯，你们的项目完成得非常出色……
